title: Add stratified noise calibrator and adaptive probe scheduler for low-signal canaries
author: Anika Rao
description: Context: Our canary detector has been producing noisy alerts for low-volume / heterogenous traffic slices (short queries, long queries, browser vs API) leading to unnecessary rollbacks. Motivation: reduce false positives and speed up meaningful detection in low-signal cohorts without increasing probe cost. This PR introduces two complementary components: (1) Stratified Noise Calibrator (SNC) — a per-stratum robust noise estimator that derives baseline variance and Minimal Detectable Effect (MDE) using median-absolute-deviation + IQR trimming and an empirical noise model; and (2) Adaptive Probe Scheduler (APS) — a probe allocation layer that dynamically assigns probe budget to strata based on expected information gain (posterior variance reduction) and the user's rollout priority hints. Approach: SNC computes noise baselines per stratum (user_cohort, model_variant, sequence_length_bucket) and emits metrics (perf_canary.noise_baseline, perf_canary.mde_estimate). APS queries SNC and current traffic rates, computes expected value-of-information, then increments probe rates for strata where MDE > configured detection target or where posterior uncertainty dominates. Both pieces are integrated into the rollout guard: when aggregate confidence is below threshold, APS will increase probes up to a capped budget and, if uncertainty persists, the guard will hold or throttle the canary. Statistical protection: SNC applies Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction across strata to control multi-comparison false alarms and exposes a confidence score to the guard. Implementation notes: core logic implemented in Go in go/perf/canary; metrics and alerts via Prometheus rules; simulator and integration scenarios in py/tools/canary_simulator to reproduce 0.5%–5% regressions per cohort. Tests: unit tests for SNC math, APS allocation policy, and a small-scale end-to-end simulation that runs in CI (simulated traffic with deterministic RNG seeds). Backwards compatibility: default behavior is off; rollout policy must opt-in via canary.config.alpha.enable_stratified_calibrator = true. Checklist: [x] design doc linked (Linear ENG-5421) [x] unit tests [x] integration simulator scenarios [x] Prometheus recording rules and alert templates [x] docs and runbook [x] migration notes for existing canary dashboards. Risks & mitigations: metric cardinality — strata keys are canonicalized and capped to configured cardinality; noisy short-lived cohorts — APS applies minimum probe windows to avoid churn. Open questions: tune default MDE multiplier for PLG customers (left conservative).

release_notes: Added an opt-in stratified noise calibration and adaptive probe scheduler to improve canary detection in low-signal traffic. Operators must enable canary.config.alpha.enable_stratified_calibrator to use. Provides new Prometheus metrics perf_canary.noise_baseline and perf_canary.mde_estimate; includes runbook and dashboards.
notes_for_ops: Default disabled. If enabling in production, start with mde_multiplier=2.5 and cardinality_cap=50; monitor perf_canary.noise_baseline and perf_canary.probe_allocations and watch for increase in probe traffic. Use runbook docs/runbooks/canary-calibration.md for rollback steps.
